title: Schwinger-Keldysh effective actions for non-hydrodynamic poles and branch cuts
authors: Andrea Amoretti, Matteo Anselmi, Daniel K. Brattan
abstract: Retarded thermal correlators, analytically continued to complex frequency, exhibit non-hydrodynamic poles and branch cuts that constrain hydrodynamics. We construct Gaussian Schwinger-Keldysh effective actions in which branch cuts arise from continua of relaxation poles and response functions are governed by Stieltjes transforms of relaxation-time densities. Dynamical KMS symmetry, positivity and stability constrain the spectra, while endpoint behaviour controls the local branch structure and near-edge pole scaling. The illustrative examples of uniform and power-law densities exhibit respectively beyond-all-orders pole-endpoint separation and a continuous interpolation between pole-pole and pole-branch-point termination. Finally, we show that an energy-dependent relaxation-time approximation in kinetic theory provides a microscopic realization of our branch cuts at zero momentum.
summary: This work develops a theoretical framework using Schwinger-Keldysh effective actions to describe thermal relaxation in systems exhibiting complex spectral features like branch cuts. By extending the model from discrete relaxation modes to continuous spectra, the authors derive transport coefficients and show how these non-hydrodynamic features constrain the system's dynamics. This provides a powerful tool for analyzing non-equilibrium quantum transport.
main_problem: The paper constructs Schwinger-Keldysh effective actions to rigorously incorporate non-hydrodynamic poles and branch cuts that govern the relaxation dynamics of thermal systems.
main_result: The theory successfully models the transition from discrete relaxation spectra to continuous branch cuts, providing closed-form expressions for transport coefficients like conductivity.
method: The analysis employs the Schwinger-Keldysh formalism, utilizing Gaussian effective actions and analyzing the resulting spectral properties via complex frequency continuation.
model_or_system: The system models a thermal medium undergoing relaxation of conserved densities, extended from a simple U(1) current to include additional vector fields (Maxwell-Cattaneo type extension).
key_observables: Retarded thermal correlators, optical conductivity ($\sigma(\omega, \vec{k})$), and the structure of the effective action $S_{MC}$.
important_parameters: Relaxation time density ($	au$), complex frequency ($\omega$), and momentum ($\vec{k}$); the analysis distinguishes between hydrodynamic and non-hydrodynamic poles.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the Gaussian order of the effective action, and approximations like the energy-diagonal Relaxation-Time Approximation (RTA) are used for microscopic realization.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the structure of branch cuts parameterized by relaxation time ($	au$) and show the derived transport coefficients for transverse and longitudinal responses.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first setting up the SK action for relaxation fields, then generalizing the spectrum from discrete poles to a continuous density ($	au$), and finally deriving the transport coefficients and the effective action using techniques like the Schur complement.
why_interesting: The rigorous treatment of non-equilibrium dynamics, especially the incorporation of continuous spectral features (branch cuts) into effective actions, is crucial for understanding transport in strongly coupled, non-equilibrium quantum systems.
